newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power talked up with cold, cash natgas.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power talked up with cold, cash natgas.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) district were talked sharply higher Tuesday amid forecasts for very cold weather and a jump in physical natural gas prices.
"Loads are going to be way up tomorrow. There's just not a lot of power available," a Houston marketer said.
Temperatures through the state were predicted to be 15 to 30 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal Wednesday with slight moderation possibly on Friday, which would still run 10 to 15 degrees below normal.
Extended outlook showed below-normal temperatures would remain in the region at least until the early part of next week.

Swing gas prices in south Texas jumped to the $4.40-$4.50 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range after discussed as high as $4.70. Today's prices jumped another 50 cents from Monday's range in the $3.90s to low-$4.
Amid strength in the gas market, some Texas utilities were said to likely switch on combustion turbines using diesel fuel to meet peak demand periods, market sources said.
Bids and offers for next-day ERCOT electricity were discussed in an extremely wide range today with almost no trades reported.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Wednesday delivery were assessed at $45.00-$70.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $42.00-43.00 Monday.
Non-firm peak power for Wednesday was notationally pegged at $42.00-$60.00, against Monday's quote of $40.00-41.00.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Wednesday were talked in the $30.00-$40.00 range, up $10.00-$20.00 from Monday's $17.00-19.00.
Non-firm off-peak ERCOT power for Wednesday was notationally assessed at $25.00-$35.00, sharply higher than $14.00-16.00 Monday.
ERCOT power for the rest of December was quoted in the $44.00-$50.00 area. ERCOT January/February peak prices climbed to $41.00-$43.00, up from Monday's $38.00-39.00.
